newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBM'S JAPAN UNIT TO CUT HOME-USE PC PRICES.
newsitem.headline: IBM'S JAPAN UNIT TO CUT HOME-USE PC PRICES.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp's (IBM) Japan unit said on Monday that the company would cut wholesale prices of home-use personal computers by 10 to 15 percent across-the-board.
The cutback reflects lower prices for Intel Corp's Pentium microprocessors, an IBM Japan spokesman said.
IBM Japan currently sells three types of individual-use PCs in the Japanese market. The first type are Aptiva-line desktop PCs and the other two are lines of ThinkPad brand notebook PCs.
Despite a steady increase in demand for upper-end corporate-use PCs, sales of individual-use PCs, particularly those of desktop PCs, have slowed as a result of price increases late last year.
The spokesman said the price cuts would help IBM Japan achieve its target of boosting individual-use PC shipments by 30 percent in 1997/98.
Shipments of personal computers in Japan in the April-June period showed a rise of four percent from the same period last year to 1.7 million units, a trade body announced earlier this month.
In contrast, PC shipments in the same period last year had shown a 51 percent year-on-year increase.
